13 A shelf PQ is attached to a vertical wall at P and supports a book.
The shelf is held horizontal by a rigid bar XY, as shown.

wall

The weight of the shelf is Ws and the weight of the book is Wb.
The bar is at an angle  to the shelf and exerts a force F on the shelf.
The shelf is in equilibrium.
What are the magnitudes of the horizontal and the vertical components of the force of the wall on
the shelf at P?
horizontal component
vertical component
A
F cos 
(Ws + Wb – F cos  )
B
F cos 
(Ws + Wb – F sin  )
C
F sin 
(Ws + Wb – F cos  )
D
F sin 
(Ws + Wb – F sin  )

hints: Look at the angle $\theta$ between the bar and the horizontal shelf to decide which part of $F$ is $F\cos\theta$ and which is $F\sin\theta$.
Recall that for the shelf in equilibrium the resultant horizontal force must be zero and the resultant vertical force must be zero.
Let the wall supply a horizontal force to cancel the horizontal push of the bar, and a vertical force that plus the upward $F\sin\theta$ supports $W_s + W_b$.
walkthrough: List the forces on the shelf: weights $W_s$ and $W_b$ vertically down, force $F$ along the bar from the strut, and unknown horizontal and vertical forces from the wall at P.
Resolve $F$, which is at angle $\theta$ to the horizontal shelf, into components: horizontal component $F\cos\theta$ and vertical upward component $F\sin\theta$.
Apply horizontal equilibrium: sum of horizontal forces equals zero, so the wall must exert an equal and opposite horizontal force of magnitude $F\cos\theta$.
Apply vertical equilibrium: upward forces equal downward forces, so $P_{vertical} + F\sin\theta = W_s + W_b$.
The pair $F\cos\theta$ and $(W_s + W_b - F\sin\theta)$ matches the table. This is option B.

A.explanation: Horizontal part $F\cos\theta$ is correct, but the vertical part of $F$ is $F\sin\theta$, not $F\cos\theta$.

B.explanation: Horizontal balance needs $F\cos\theta$ from the wall and vertical balance gives $(W_s + W_b - F\sin\theta)$ upward from the wall.

C.explanation: Both parts swap sine and cosine: the horizontal part along the shelf is $F\cos\theta$ and the vertical part is $F\sin\theta$.

D.explanation: Vertical part is correct but the horizontal component of $F$ at angle $\theta$ to the horizontal is $F\cos\theta$, not $F\sin\theta$.
